scope: Informational intent only. Both compounds have written records of their own, so component questions about dose and form are redirected there rather than duplicated here.
stage0_note: The record holds two head-to-head claims and both are animal work: a toxicity screen in mouse embryonic stem cells, and a rat transcriptome study of Pro-Gly-Pro, the tripeptide both compounds carry at one end. The second is not a comparison but it is the most interesting fact about the pair, and the guide uses it.

h1: Selank vs semax: two Russian peptides built on the same tail, tested for different things, and never compared
dek: One came from a fragment of ACTH and was studied in stroke and attention; the other from a fragment of an immune peptide and was studied in anxiety. Both carry the same tripeptide at one end, both are approved only in Russia, and almost everything sold in the West is a modified version that no trial has tested.

Is semax useful for ADHD?
queries.answer: No trial has tested semax for ADHD as it is diagnosed outside Russia. The attention findings come from Russian studies in children with what those papers call minimal brain dysfunction and from cognitive measures in other conditions. The interest is real and the evidence is not the kind a regulator would accept for that indication.

queries.heading: What is actually sold: the acetylated and amidated versions
queries.boundary: Almost everything sold in the West is not the compound the trials studied. N-acetyl semax amidate and N-acetyl selank amidate are modified versions, and no trial has tested either.

queries.heading: Side effects, and how thin the safety evidence is
queries.boundary: Both are described as well tolerated in small Russian trials. Neither has a modern safety study, neither has been tested for long-term use, and the products people actually buy are not the ones those trials used.

How long do they last?
queries.answer: Both are short-acting, which is why the nasal route and repeated daily dosing are used. The parent peptides are broken down quickly in plasma, and their shared C-terminal tripeptide is itself active, so what circulates after a dose is not only the molecule that was given. No modern pharmacokinetic study of either is in this record's ledger.

queries.heading: How long do they last?
How does semax compare with noopept?
queries.answer: Noopept is a different thing: a synthetic dipeptide-like compound taken orally, also developed in Russia, and also lacking approval elsewhere. It has its own small Russian trial literature. No study has compared it with semax, and the same caution applies to both, that the evidence base is a national one that has not been replicated internationally.

information_gain: The only page on this query that explains what the two compounds share, which is not a mechanism but a design: both are a short active fragment with the tripeptide Pro-Gly-Pro attached to protect it, and one of the two studies naming both is about that tripeptide's own activity in the brain. The only page to separate the trial record by what each was actually tested for, stroke, optic-nerve disease and attention for semax, anxiety disorders for selank, with the study sizes, which are small. The only page to state that N-acetyl semax amidate and N-acetyl selank amidate, the forms actually sold in the West and drawing 1,221 searches a month of their own, are modified molecules with no trial evidence behind them. And the only page to answer the combining question with what exists, which is a mouse stem-cell screen and a rat transcriptome study.
serp_format_rewarded: A cited comparison with tables. The ranking pages are clinic explainers with one to seven citations and no trial detail, and a PubMed abstract sits at seventh, so the query tolerates primary literature. The gaps are the trial table, the acetylated forms and the absence of any comparison.
